name: Archpoet
bio: The Archpoet (Archipoeta) is the name given to an anonymous Latin poet of the twelfth century, probably born around 1130, who belonged to the wandering clerics and students known as goliards. He appears to have been a knight's son from the German lands, trained in the schools, who served in the household of Rainald of Dassel, imperial chancellor to Frederick Barbarossa and archbishop-elect of Cologne, and followed him on the emperor's Italian campaigns of the early 1160s.

Ten poems survive under his pseudonym, among them petitions to Rainald for money and a cloak, a eulogy of Frederick and his victories over Milan, and the famous Confession (‘Estuans intrinsecus’), which is held in the archive in the Carmina Burana. Written in rhymed accentual Latin verse, his work mixes tavern wit and scriptural parody with learned classical allusion.
